papers.title_in_file: Gibbs Sampling of Continuous Potentials on a Quantum Computer
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, statements of Theorems 3.2 and 3.3, Section 4 results discussion, Conclusion; appendices not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper giving a quantum algorithm for Gibbs sampling of periodic continuous potentials via quantum Fourier transforms and the Fokker-Planck equation.

assertions.value: The authors state that their algorithm makes zeroeth order queries to a quantum oracle of the function and achieves polynomial quantum speedups in mean estimation in the Gibbs measure for generic non-convex periodic functions.
quotes: Our algorithm makes zeroeth order queries to a quantum oracle of the function and achieves polynomial quantum speedups in mean estimation in the Gibbs measure for generic non-convex periodic functions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract statement of a complexity result; the speedup is relative to classical upper bounds the authors cite, not to a classical lower bound.
assertions.reader_inference: The speedup is a comparison of query-count upper bounds, not a proved separation from all classical algorithms.

assertions.value: The authors state that comparing their query counts with a classical Riemannian Langevin bound suggests an exponential quantum speedup in the sampling precision and a quartic speedup in the precision of mean estimation, for Morse functions on tori.
quotes: This suggests an exponential quantum speedup in the sampling precision, and a quartic speedup in the precision of mean estimation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors word it as 'suggests'; a comparison of upper bounds.

assertions.value: The authors state that directly solving for the steady state of the Fokker-Planck equation requires solving linear systems with exponentially poor condition numbers, so they integrate for a long time and do not achieve a shortcut to the problem of long mixing time in equilibrium dynamics.
quotes: directly solving for the steady state of the FPE requires solving linear systems with exponentially poor condition numbers
not achieve a shortcut to the problem of long mixing time in equilibrium dynamics.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in the Introduction, p.1-2.

assertions.value: The authors state that they consider periodic boundary conditions because these allow quantum Fourier transforms, and so focus on potentials defined on high dimensional tori.
quotes: In this paper we consider periodic boundary conditions since they allow us to leverage quantum Fourier transforms.
we focus on potentials defined on high dimensional tori.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope, Introduction p.2.
assertions.reader_inference: Results do not directly cover non-periodic or unbounded potentials; the paper adds a Chebyshev extension in an appendix that was not read.

papers.title_in_file: Accelerating Feedback-based Algorithms for Quantum Optimization Using Gradient Descent
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, experimental setup and results discussion, Conclusion; Preliminaries and method derivation skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of GD-QLC, a hybrid of FALQON feedback control with per-layer gradient descent, for combinatorial optimization.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in classical simulations, GD-QLC consistently outperforms FALQON across a range of problem sizes and problem classes, in both approximation ratio and success probability.
quotes: we demonstrated that GD-QLC consistently outperforms FALQON across a range of problem sizes
Across all problem classes and sizes considered, the results demonstrate that GD-QLC consistently outperforms FALQON
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one set of classical simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that all experiments were performed using classical simulations, and that they do not include standard QAOA baselines in their experimental comparisons.
quotes: All experiments were performed using classical simulations
We do not include standard QAOA baselines in our experimental comparisons
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of experimental scope, Section 4, p.5.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against FALQON and a second-order FALQON variant only.

assertions.value: The authors state that larger problem sizes were not computationally tractable within classical simulation limits, and that experimental validation on quantum hardware remains a direction for future work.
quotes: Larger problem sizes were not computationally tractable within classical simulation limits.
Finally, experimental validation on quantum hardware and applications to broader classes of optimization and control problems remain important directions for future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit in Section 4 and Section 5.

papers.title_in_file: QML-HCS: A Hypercausal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Non-Stationary Environments
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Framework Overview, experiment section, Conclusion; implementation detail sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A software-framework paper describing a quantum-inspired (classically simulated) hypercausal ML library with a minimal drift simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in one simulated run with injected hardware-style drift, the aggregate loss and the coherence component remain bounded and stable.
quotes: Both remain bounded and stable despite the injected physical drift
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-run simulation described qualitatively from figures; no baseline comparison.
assertions.reader_inference: No comparison against any other model is reported in the sections read, so the result does not show an advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the framework is quantum-inspired, runs without specialized hardware, and that the experiment used a state dimension of 7, 20 branches and 300 epochs.
quotes: enabling experimentation in quantum-inspired learning, causal reasoning, and hybrid computation without the need for specialized hardware.
We instantiate a hypercausal model with a state dimension D = 7, K = 20 branches, and T = 300 epochs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its setup, Section V.A.
assertions.reader_inference: The work is classical simulation of a quantum-inspired model, not a quantum algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors state that this release emphasizes architectural clarity and minimal validation, and that comprehensive benchmarking and theoretical formalization are left to future research.
quotes: While this work emphasizes architectural clarity and minimal validation, future research will extend the system with comprehensive benchmarking, theoretical formalization
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit in the Introduction.

papers.title_in_file: Extending the Frontiers of QNLP Beyond English: Grammar-Sensitive Pipeline for Hindi Sentiment Classification Using Compositional Quantum Models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Background, parts of Dataset and Methodology, Results and Discussion, Conclusion, Future Scope
papers.what_it_is: An application paper building a Hindi pregroup-grammar QNLP pipeline with Lambeq and a hybrid quantum-classical network, evaluated in simulation on a small Hindi corpus.

assertions.value: The authors report that binary-class performance was consistently stronger than ternary-class performance, and that the 80:10:10 split yielded higher accuracy than the 70:10:20 split for both tasks.
assertions.anchor: Section 5, p.12, Table 3 (numeric accuracies are in the table only)
quotes: As shown in Table 3, performance in the Binary-class classification task was consistently stronger than in the Ternary-class version
the comparison of dataset splits reveals that the 80:10:10 configuration yielded higher accuracy than the 70:10:20 split for both tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small study.
assertions.reader_inference: The text reports no classical baseline in the sections read, so the quantum contribution is not isolated.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation used a manually annotated corpus of 250 Hindi sentences and that all models were trained and tested using simulated quantum circuits.
quotes: when evaluated on a manually annotated corpus of 250 Hindi sentences
All models were trained and tested using simulated quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own data and setup, Sections 5 and 6.

assertions.value: The authors state that to date all experiments have been conducted on simulated or hybrid quantum platforms and that running on real quantum processors is a future step.
quotes: To date, all experiments have been conducted on simulated or hybrid quantum platforms
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit in Section 7.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the compositional QNLP method successfully detects Hindi semantic features, including intricate morphological patterns and negation-induced semantic transformations.
quotes: The compositional QNLP method successfully detects Hindi semantic features, including intricate morphological patterns and negation-induced semantic transformations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author conclusion; the sections read report overall accuracy only, with no ablation isolating negation.
assertions.reader_inference: Partial read: I did not find a negation-specific test in the sections read.

papers.title_in_file: Explicit quantum surrogates for quantum kernel models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, summary of results, Conclusion and parts of the appendix discussion; derivations and most appendices not read
papers.what_it_is: A method paper converting a trained quantum-kernel (implicit) model into an explicit parameterized-circuit model, tested in numerical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the prediction accuracy of the explicit quantum surrogate decreases by less than 0.010 compared to trained implicit models on the MNISQ and VQE-generated datasets.
quotes: decreases by less than 0.010 compared to trained implicit models
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result on two datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that a scaling analysis shows EQS initialization suppresses the exponential decay of gradients seen in randomly initialized circuits, with the performance gap widening to more than 5 orders of magnitude at 16 qubits.
quotes: A scaling analysis reveals that the EQS initialization suppresses the exponential decay of gradients observed in randomly initialized circuits, with the performance gap widening to more than 5 orders of magnitude at 16 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result, up to the stated qubit count.
assertions.reader_inference: A larger initial gradient is not the same as better final trainability; the paper's own wording is 'a path to mitigate'.

assertions.value: The authors state that performance is evaluated through numerical simulations and that the two-step construction constitutes the main source of a one-time resource cost.
quotes: We evaluate the performance of EQS for classification tasks through numerical simulations.
This two-step construction process, while powerful, constitutes the main source of the one-time resource cost for our framework.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope and cost, Introduction p.2.

papers.title_in_file: Comparative Analysis of Black Hole Mass Estimation in Type-2 AGNs: Classical vs. Quantum Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Dataset section, Discussion, Conclusion; literature survey and per-model result tables skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A benchmark comparing classical ML/DL regressors with simulated quantum ML regressors for black hole mass estimation on SDSS DR7 Type-2 AGN data.

assertions.value: The authors report that classical algorithms gave better results than the quantum models, that the best classical model (LSTM) reached an accuracy of 99.77%, and that the best quantum model (Estimator-QNN) reached an MSE of 0.0124 and an accuracy of 99.75%.
quotes: The results revealed that classical algorithms gave better
Among the classical models, LSTM has the best result with an accuracy of 99.77%.
Estimator-QNN has the highest accuracy for quantum algorithms with an MSE of 0.0124 and an accuracy of 99.75%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one dataset, simulated quantum models.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper's 'accuracy' appears to be a percentage derived from an error metric, not classification accuracy. The Introduction says classical was 'slightly better' while the Conclusion says the gap 'remains significant'.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dataset comes from SDSS Data Release 7, covering approximately 10,000 Type-2 AGN spectra, and that the quantum models were run in simulation rather than on real quantum hardware.
quotes: We have sourced the dataset from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Data Release 7 (DR7) which focuses on approximately 10,000 Type-2 Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) spectra.
In our study, we rely on quantum simulations rather than real quantum hardware to explore the performance of QML algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its data and setup, Sections 4.2 and 6.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because the quantum models were simulated, the results appear idealized and do not fully reflect the behavior of quantum algorithms in real-world conditions, and that inefficient encoding of classical data into quantum states is a significant limitation.
quotes: the results appear idealized and do not fully reflect the behavior of quantum algorithms in real-world conditions
Another significant limitation is the inefficiency of encoding classical data into quantum states, especially for large datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limits in the Discussion.

papers.title_in_file: Unsupervised Techniques to Detect Quantum Chaos
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections II and III, Discussion and Conclusions; Sections IV and V details skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A condensed-matter numerics paper using a classical Self-Organizing Map to detect the integrable-to-chaotic transition from a random-graph Hamiltonian matrix.

assertions.value: The authors state that, using Self-Organizing Maps, they presented some evidence that unsupervised neural networks can detect the chaos to integrability transition without eigenvalues or eigenvectors, in excellent agreement with spectral r-ratios.
quotes: Using Self-Organizing Maps we presented some evidence that this is indeed possible and that the predictions of the neural network are in excellent agreement with conventional spectral methods
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result for one family of Hamiltonians; authors say 'some evidence'.
assertions.reader_inference: A classical neural network on quantum-physics matrices; no quantum computer or quantum ML algorithm is involved.

assertions.value: The authors report that the spectral r-ratios show a transition from integrability to chaos as the rewiring probability of small-world Watts-Strogatz graphs is increased, seemingly around p = 0.02.
quotes: The r-ratios show a transition from integrability to chaos as the rewiring probability is increased, and the transition seems to happen around p = 0.02, see Figure 2.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result for one model family.

assertions.value: The authors state that one possible scenario is that the SOM is not detecting the chaos to integrability transition but a change in the geometry of the graph.
quotes: The second scenario is that the SOM is not detecting the chaos/integrable transition, but it is detecting the change in geometry of the graph.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state this unresolved alternative explanation in the Discussion.

papers.title_in_file: From Reachability to Learnability: Geometric Design Principles for Quantum Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 5 benchmarking and results, Summary and Conclusions; Sections 2 to 4 derivations and appendices not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A theory-plus-benchmark paper giving a geometric criterion (aCLS) for when a quantum neural network layer can learn features.

assertions.value: The authors state that, within their framework, data-independent trainable unitaries are complete but non-selective, pure data encodings are selective but non-tunable, and hence geometric flexibility requires a non-trivial joint dependence on data and trainable weights.
quotes: we show that data-independent trainable unitaries are complete but non-selective
Hence, geometric flexibility requires a non-trivial joint dependence on data and trainable weights.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as shown results in the pure-state setting (Sections 2 to 4; proofs in Appendix A); I read the abstract and conclusions, not the proofs.

assertions.value: The authors report that numerical examples show aCLS-satisfying data re-uploading models outperforming non-tunable schemes while requiring only a quarter of the gate operations, with consistent one-vs-all AUC improvements across all classes on the multi-class JetClass benchmark.
quotes: Numerical examples validate that aCLS-satisfying data re-uploading models outperform non-tunable schemes while requiring only a quarter of the gate operations.
on the multi-class JetClass benchmark, we observe consistent one-vs-all AUC improvements across all classes
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation results on toy and collider datasets; AUC values are in tables only.
assertions.reader_inference: The baseline is pure data re-uploading only, not other QNN designs or classical models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the analysis is carried out in the pure-state setting and that extending the geometric view beyond the present pure-state closed-system setting is future work.
quotes: We study this question in the pure-state setting
motivate extending this geometric learning viewpoint beyond the present pure-state closed-system setting.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope, Abstract and Section 6.
